children: “Verity” easily topped the domestic box office with an estimated $32.6 million opening, but moviegoing was otherwise subdued as the overall weekend failed to reach $100 million.

The domestic marketplace generated an estimated $99 million from Friday through Sunday, down 21% from the previous weekend, according to Rentrak’s Paul Dergarabedian. The showing was nevertheless 14.8% better than the comparable weekend last year, while the top 10 films combined for $91.6 million.

“Verity,” starring Dakota Johnson, Anne Hathaway and Josh Hartnett, accounted for nearly one-third of all domestic ticket sales by itself. The psychological thriller opened in 3,510 locations for an average of $9,293 per theater. It added $30 million from 70 international markets, giving it a $62.5 million worldwide opening.
The drop-off after “Verity” was steep. Sony’s
“Resident Evil” placed second with $12.5 million in its third weekend, down 46%, while Paramount’s
“Heart of the Beast” earned $11 million in its second weekend, down 45%. No other movie reached $10 million.

The overall domestic marketplace generated an estimated $99 million for the Oct. 2-4 weekend. That was down 21% from the previous weekend but 14.8% higher than the comparable frame last year. The top 10 movies accounted for about $91.6 million.

For theater operators and Hollywood studios, the bigger story remains the strength of the 2026 recovery. Domestic ticket sales have reached $7.949 billion through Oct. 4, up 19.5% from $6.654 billion at the same point last year. The industry is now about $50.8 million short of $8 billion and is projected to cross that threshold around Oct. 9, depending on weekday ticket sales. September contributed $601.9 million, up 1.3% from a year earlier.
and DreamWorks Animation’s “Forgotten Island” ranked sixth with $7.2 million, bringing its domestic total to $23.6 million and worldwide haul to $38.5 million. Disney

and Marvel’s “Avengers Endgame: Encore” followed with $4.4 million in its second weekend. The re-release has now generated $126 million worldwide, pushing the film’s lifetime global box office, including its original run, to nearly $2.93 billion.

Zee Studios International’s “Drishyam - The Conclusion” had a notable showing in limited release, earning $2.74 million from only 541 locations for an average of $5,070 per theater. Warner Bros.’ “Practical Magic 2” took ninth with $2.66 million and reached $100 million in worldwide ticket sales.

Sony’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” rounded out the top 10 with $2.45 million in its 10th weekend. The superhero movie has now amassed $954.5 million domestically and a studio-reported $2.506 billion worldwide.

title: ‘Verity’ leads tepid box office weekend with $33M debut
